chunks: We were told by Muhammad ibn Musa ibn al-Mutawakkil, who said: He told me Muhammad ibn Yahya al-Attar, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from those he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) who said:

A man said in his presence: 'Allah is Greater.' So he said: 'Allah is Greater than what thing?' Then he said: 'Than everything.' Then Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'You have limited Him.' Then the man said: 'And how shall I say?' So he said: 'Allah is Greater than to be described.'
ai.seo_question: What is the correct way to say 'Allah is Greater' according to Imam al-Sadiq?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Ma'ani al-Akhbar*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) refines the theological understanding of *Allahu Akbar* by distinguishing between comparative greatness, which implies limitation through relation to creation, and absolute transcendence. He guides the companion to affirm that God is 'greater than to be described,' emphasizing *tanzih* (divine incomparability) over *tashbih* (anthropomorphism). This highlights the Shia scholarly emphasis on precise linguistic formulation to preserve God's infinite nature against human conceptual constraints.

en.basel-kadem: 2.	We were told by Muhammed bin Musa bin Mutawakkil, that he said: We were told by Muhammed bin Yahya al-‘Attar, from Sahl bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahbub, from those he mentioned, from Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, that he said:

A man said in his presence: Allah is Greater. So he said: Allah is Greater than what thing? Then he said: Than everything. Then Abu Abdillah, peace be upon him, said: You have limited Him. Then the man said: And how shall I say? So he said: Allah is Greater than to be described.
